newsitem.title: USA: Casinos object to N.J. tunnel proposal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Casinos object to N.J. tunnel proposal - paper.

text.p: Some of Atlantic City's largest casino operators are objecting to a proposed tunnel project for the city because they say it favors competitors, the Star Ledger reported Thursday.
Representatives of MGM Grand Inc and Sun International Hotels Ltd said the proposed development favors casinos being planned across town from their hotels.
The state is planning to spend $330 million on a highway and tunnel to improve access to the marina district, where three new casinos expected to cost about $2 billion are planned.
The major parties reached agreement last month on the tunnel plan, but existing casino operators said the most recent draft differs from the one they signed off on in January, the paper reported.
Officials of the South Jersey Transportation Authority, which is contributing to the tunnel financing, will meet with the casino operators this week to discuss the issue.
